input_signals.name: EVYieldCleanWorkingCapital
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(ebitda, ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), SUB(ADD(dltt, dlc), che))), NEG(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Enterprise-level cheapness (EBITDA/EV) is trustworthy only when operating profitability is not being manufactured by working-capital build-ups in receivables and inventory.
input_signals.reasoning: EBITDA/EV neutralizes leverage and cash holdings so cheapness is measured on operating assets, while the change in non-cash working capital captures the specific accrual channel (receivables/inventory inflation) that contaminates EBITDA. Combining them should separate genuinely cheap operating businesses from those whose EBITDA is a working-capital illusion.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( ratio( ebitda, add( mul( prcc_f, csho ), sub( add( dltt, dlc ), che ) ) ), neg( ratio( delta( sub( sub( act, che ), sub( lct, dlc ) ), 1 ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: ValueCleanSloanAccruals
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), NEG(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(wcap, 1), dp), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Book-to-market earns a premium only when reported profits are not produced by working-capital build-up net of depreciation; accrual-heavy cheap firms are value traps.
input_signals.reasoning: The accrual leg is the balance-sheet Sloan measure (change in working capital minus depreciation) scaled by assets, built from theme-exclusive items `wcap` and `dp` that are reported far more broadly than cash-flow-statement components, which should lift coverage well above the 0.11 of the accepted gen-0 signal. Ranking both legs makes the long book cheap-and-clean and the short book expensive-and-accrual-laden, the exact intersection the economic story requires.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( ratio( ceq, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), neg( ratio( sub( delta( wcap, 1 ), dp ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: SloanCashEarningsYield
input_signals.expression: RATIO(SUB(ADD(ib, dp), DELTA(wcap, 1)), MUL(prcc_f, csho))
input_signals.hypothesis: The correct value multiple is price relative to accrual-purged cash earnings; firms cheap on cash earnings outperform, and firms that look cheap only on GAAP income do not.
input_signals.reasoning: Instead of blending two ranks, this embeds the accrual correction inside the valuation ratio itself, so accruals change the measured cheapness rather than acting as a separate filter — a distinguishable structural test against Signal 1. Using `dp` and `DELTA(wcap,1)` keeps coverage high while making the numerator an approximation of cash flow available to equity.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ratio( sub( add( ib, dp ), delta( wcap, 1 ) ), mul( prcc_f, csho ) )

input_signals.name: CheapAndCleanConjunction
input_signals.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(wcap, 1), dp), at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Value and accounting quality are complements, not substitutes: a firm must be both cheap and cash-backed to earn the premium, so the weaker of the two ranks should govern expected returns.
input_signals.reasoning: SUMRANK lets an extreme value rank compensate for terrible accruals (and vice versa), whereas MIN enforces the conjunction and should sharpen the long leg toward genuine quality-value names. Comparing this against Signal 1 isolates the aggregation choice while holding the underlying economic channels fixed, telling us whether the FF5 alpha comes from the intersection or from linear averaging.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( rank( ratio( ceq, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), rank( neg( ratio( sub( delta( wcap, 1 ), dp ), at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: CumulativeBloatValue
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), NEG(TS_SUM(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(wcap, 1), dp), at), 5)))
input_signals.hypothesis: What contaminates cheapness is not a single year's accrual but a multi-year accumulation of unconfirmed accruals (balance-sheet bloat), which must eventually be reversed or written off.
input_signals.reasoning: A five-year cumulative accrual sum captures the stock of soft assets embedded in book equity, which is exactly why a high book-to-market can be illusory — the book value itself is inflated. This changes the economic channel from annual earnings quality to the reliability of the denominator-free book anchor, a mechanism a one-year accrual cannot express.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( ratio( ceq, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), neg( ts_sum( ratio( sub( delta( wcap, 1 ), dp ), at ), 5 ) ) )

input_signals.name: SalesYieldRevenueQuality
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(sale, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), NEG(GROWTH(RATIO(SUB(act, che), sale), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Sales-to-price cheapness is trustworthy only if revenue is converting to cash; rising non-cash current assets per dollar of sales signals channel-stuffing or inventory accumulation that will reverse.
input_signals.reasoning: This swaps the valuation anchor to a revenue multiple (immune to earnings management in the numerator) and pairs it with an operating-quality ratio measuring how many non-cash current assets are needed to generate a dollar of sales, a distinct accrual channel from net income minus cash flow. If sales-based value works better than book- or earnings-based value once revenue quality is imposed, the interaction is about revenue recognition rather than earnings smoothing.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( ratio( sale, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), neg( growth( ratio( sub( act, che ), sale ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: IndNeutralCleanValue
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), NEG(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(wcap, 1), dp), at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Cross-industry differences in normal book-to-market and normal accrual intensity (capital-intensive versus working-capital-intensive sectors) contaminate the raw composite; within-industry cheapness backed by within-industry clean accounting is the real mispricing.
input_signals.reasoning: This holds the economic channels of ValueCleanSloanAccruals fixed and changes only the neutralization, so it cleanly diagnoses whether the negative FF5 alpha came from industry-level value/investment tilts absorbed by HML and CMA. If alpha turns positive, industry neutralization is the design lever worth consolidating in later generations.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( ind_zscore( ratio( ceq, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), neg( ind_zscore( ratio( sub( delta( wcap, 1 ), dp ), at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: ConservativeDepreciationValue
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(dp, at))
input_signals.hypothesis: Cheapness is more credible when accounting is conservative: firms charging heavy depreciation understate current earnings and book value, so their low price reflects accounting conservatism rather than genuine economic decline.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the working-capital accrual channel with the long-lived-asset accrual channel — depreciation adequacy — which is a distinct source of earnings quality and is not what the Sloan measure captures. It also uses only current-year levels, so it should show whether the archive's stuck 0.11 coverage is driven by the two-year requirement of DELTA(wcap, 1).
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( ratio( ceq, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), ratio( dp, at ) )

input_signals.name: HardBookToMarket
input_signals.expression: RATIO(SUB(ceq, SUB(SUB(act, che), lct)), MUL(prcc_f, csho))
input_signals.hypothesis: A high book-to-market is only informative if book equity is composed of hard assets (cash and fixed capital) rather than soft accrual assets; stripping non-cash working capital out of book equity should isolate defensible value.
input_signals.reasoning: Rather than filtering value with a separate quality score, this repairs the value measure's numerator, so the resulting spread is a *different* value factor rather than HML plus a quality tilt — a structurally distinct route to non-spanned alpha. Soft-asset-heavy book equity is exactly what gets written down in value traps, so removing it should shift the long leg away from the traps.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ratio( sub( ceq, sub( sub( act, che ), lct ) ), mul( prcc_f, csho ) )

input_signals.name: PayoutNotCoveredByCashEarnings
input_signals.expression: RATIO(SUB(dvc, SUB(ADD(ib, dp), DELTA(wcap, 1))), MUL(prcc_f, csho))
input_signals.hypothesis: The classic value trap is a high-yield, cheap firm distributing cash it is not generating; a dividend exceeding accrual-purged cash earnings is an unsustainable payout that precedes cuts and price declines.
input_signals.reasoning: This is a distinct mechanism — payout sustainability rather than earnings quality per se — and it is high precisely for the optically attractive names (high dividend yield, low price) that pure value screens buy, so its short leg should sit inside the value universe rather than in glamour stocks. Because both the trap and non-trap firms are cheap dividend payers, the spread should be far less HML-loaded than the earlier composites.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ratio( sub( dvc, sub( add( ib, dp ), delta( wcap, 1 ) ) ), mul( prcc_f, csho ) )

input_signals.reasoning: Gen-0's EV/EBITDA composite remains the best joint result in the archive (FMB 3.59, alpha ≈ 0, Sharpe 0.29) but used a fragile multi-item working-capital delta, while gen-3 showed the working-capital stock is the wrong quality variable. This version keeps the EV anchor and the accrual *change* but measures it with the compact wcap−dp Sloan definition, isolating whether measurement noise in the accrual leg was suppressing the EV composite's alpha.

input_signals.hypothesis: Cheapness is trustworthy when it is simultaneously visible in book value, backed by net cash on the balance sheet, and not manufactured by accruals; the cash channel screens out the levered value traps that dominate book-only value screens.
input_signals.reasoning: The net-cash anchor was the only channel producing positive FF5 alpha, and the book-value-plus-clean-accruals composite was among the strongest FMB slopes, so combining all three ranks tests directly whether the two forms of evidence can be obtained together rather than traded off. Ranking each channel also removes the skewness that made the raw net-cash ratio cross-sectionally weak.

input_signals.hypothesis: Revenue-based cheapness measured against total enterprise value, combined with improving cash conversion of revenue, identifies firms whose sales are real and whose capital structure does not disguise expensiveness.
input_signals.reasoning: The sales-yield plus revenue-quality channel produced the archive's best Sharpe (0.332) but a negative alpha because price-only deflation loads the long leg with highly levered value names; deflating by EV penalizes debt and tilts the long leg toward the net-cash firms that generated positive alpha. Differencing two rank-transformed yields bounds the signal, makes the sorted deciles reflect the same monotone relation the FMB slope detects, and keeps the construction nearly value-factor neutral since both legs are price-deflated yields.

input_signals.reasoning: This keeps the winning net-cash-plus-book-value frame but swaps the working-capital accrual screen for the long-lived-asset accrual channel, which had the archive's strongest FMB slope (3.98) and the highest coverage (0.137) because it needs no lagged data. input_signals.reasoning: Net cash mixes a cash-asset effect with a negative-leverage effect, and FF5 partially prices leverage through HML and CMA, so replacing net cash with gross cash-to-price cleanly attributes the +0.029 alpha to one of the two. input_signals.hypothesis: A cash-poor, levered firm paying dividends it does not earn, whose accrual-driven profits generate no tax liability, is reporting income that exists only on paper and should underperform reliably.

input_signals.hypothesis: Rather than screening cheapness with a separate accrual score, the accrual correction belongs inside the value measure itself: book equity stripped of non-cash working capital is the portion of book value that cannot be written down.
input_signals.reasoning: This embeds the quality adjustment in the numerator of the value ratio, giving the corrected value channel half the total weight instead of splitting weight between value and quality, which is a structurally different way to express the same interaction.
